newsitem.title: UK: July Brent programme up at 40.5 cargoes.
newsitem.headline: July Brent programme up at 40.5 cargoes.

text.p: The July North Sea Brent crude oil loading programme has been set at the equivalent of 40.5 cargoes, made up of 36 full cargoes and a further 2.264 million barrels in top-ups, traders said on Friday.
The June programme had scheduled 34 full cargoes plus 2.189 million barrels in top-ups.
Traders said the heavier programme in July was due to the longer month and a lighter maintenance schedule.
Maintenance shutdowns at Total's Alwyn and Dunbar platforms, in addition to long term maintenance at Shell Expro's Brent Delta platform, helped reduce June volumes.
The Delta maintenance work continue until the fourth quarter of this year.
Earlier this month, Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro), postponed a planned shutdown at the 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) Brent Bravo field from June 1-7 to August.
It also cancelled a planned shutdown due June 22-28 at the 55,000 bpd Tern field.
Shell Expro is a joint venture between Royal Duch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp.
Crude from the Brent and Ninian systems is blended at the Sullom Voe terminal on the Shetland Islands and exported as world benchmark Brent blend.
